data.analysis: T1 and T2 are complementary, not redundant: T1 targets inter-kernel topology; T2 targets the block-local reduction. But the only timing evidence is a three-sample whole-call baseline, so neither fewer launches nor fewer block synchronizations is established as the dominant opportunity. T1 should explicitly contrast its fewer-launch hypothesis with a more parallel finalization option; a single CTA reducing many partials may erase the expected gain. T2 already provides a controlled local-kernel comparison, so its role needs no change.

revisions.objective: Explore global reduction hierarchy and launch count, treating fewer launches as a hypothesis rather than a requirement. For the primary comparisons, keep the baseline intra-block reduction fixed so this tree isolates global topology. Compare a two-kernel design (input partials, then finalization writing directly to out) with a design that adds a parallel partial-reduction stage or retains a recursive hierarchy when a single-CTA finalizer has too much work. Tune tile size and partial count, and compare full-call performance rather than attributing gains from launch count alone. Handle all valid n generically; do not scan the entire large input in one CTA or specialize to listed test sizes. Use only the supplied scratch and default stream, without relying on scratch initialization. Ensure intermediate sums are exact under cancellation using int64 intermediates or proven-safe bounds, and narrow only after the true total is established. Validate all required inputs, report failed variants, and provide repeated measurements.
revisions.subject: Global reduction hierarchy and launch-count alternatives

data.shared_assumptions: The supplied target is GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3; no additional environment facts were inspected. Both trees must preserve exact results for all valid inputs, including safe intermediate sums, buffer bounds, and uninitialized scratch. The only performance evidence is the correct baseline's three full-call samples (mean 46.4832 µs); it does not isolate kernel, launch, or synchronization costs. Keep T1 focused on global hierarchy and T2 on block-local reduction, compare measured programs directly, and do not assume their gains compose.
